context:
Research-only work - no behavior changes to the codebase. Produce an
evidence-backed inventory and a set of follow-up implementation TODOs;
maintainer decides which removals to authorize.

Methodology:
  1. Source of truth for declared deps: parse `pyproject.toml` directly
     rather than relying on `uv pip list` (which includes transitive).
     Use `tomllib` in a small throwaway script under `_project/scratch/`
     if regex gets tangled by multi-line strings + env markers.
  2. Source of truth for import sites: `Grep` across the tree with the
     import-name (not package-name) for each dep. Maintain an explicit
     pkg→import-name map - there are several mismatches (pyyaml/yaml,
     psycopg2-binary/psycopg2, pillow/PIL, google-cloud-*/google.cloud.*,
     beautifulsoup4/bs4 if present). Record the map in the inventory so
     future audits reuse it.
  3. Transitive-reach classification uses `uv tree` output as ground
     truth. A dep is "transitively available" only if it appears in
     `uv tree` for a group that a live consumer module depends on.
  4. Ownership: tie every live import back to its owning benchbox
     module (e.g. `snowflake-connector-python` → `benchbox/platforms/snowflake/`).
     An extras group with zero live consumers is a FLAG-DEAD-EXTRA.
  5. Report format mirrors `docs/development/dependency-compatibility.md`
     so a reader can cross-reference cap rationale against usage.
description:
Systematic, evidence-based review of every dependency declared in the
project with the goal of pruning anything that is not absolutely required.

Motivation:
  - `pyproject.toml` declares ~15 core deps and ~50 optional-extra groups
    covering SQL platforms, cloud storage, DataFrame engines, benchmarks,
    docs, and MCP. Extras have accreted organically as platforms were
    added and it is no longer self-evident which imports are live, which
    are dead, and which are redundant with something already pulled in
    transitively.
  - Supply chain surface: every declared dep is an install target, a
    vulnerability surface, and a version-resolution constraint. Dropping
    unused deps shrinks install size, speeds CI, and reduces the matrix
    the release gate has to keep green.
  - Complements (does NOT replace) `review-dependency-upper-bounds-quarterly.yaml`.
    That item watches caps on *kept* deps for breakage; this item asks the
    prior question: does the dep belong in the manifest at all?

Scope:
  - All `[project] dependencies`, `[project.optional-dependencies]`,
    `[dependency-groups]` in `pyproject.toml`.
  - Any `uv.sources` overrides, git pins, or platform markers.
  - Any runtime imports in `benchbox/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, `docs/`
    that name a third-party package not declared in the manifest
    (the inverse check - declared-but-unused AND used-but-undeclared).

Non-goals:
  - Not a version-bump exercise. Upper-bounds review is separate.
  - Not a rewrite of extras topology. Consolidation proposals are fine,
    but execution of breaking extras renames is out of scope and would
    be split into a follow-up.
  - Does NOT touch `_binaries/` bundled C++ binaries or dsdgen/dsqgen
    toolchain - those are artifacts, not Python deps.

Deliverable:
  - A committed markdown inventory at
    `docs/development/dependency-inventory.md` listing every declared
    dep, its extras group(s), every source file that imports it, and
    a one-line justification for keeping it. Deps with no live imports
    or with justification "covered by <other dep>" are flagged as
    elimination candidates.
  - A short follow-up TODO (or set of TODOs) proposing concrete
    removals, gated on maintainer sign-off. No deps are deleted under
    this item - only inventoried and flagged.

anti_patterns.why: several deps don't match (pyyaml/yaml, psycopg2-binary/psycopg2, google-cloud-*/google.cloud.*)

anti_patterns.dont: conflate this audit with the quarterly upper-bounds review
anti_patterns.why: they answer different questions (keep-or-drop vs. cap-is-correct)

anti_patterns.dont: rely on `uv pip list` as the source of truth for declared deps
anti_patterns.why: it includes transitives and masks which extras group owns a package

anti_patterns.dont: remove any dep as part of this item
anti_patterns.why: each removal has its own test-surface and risk profile

anti_patterns.dont: treat 'no imports found' as automatic grounds for removal
anti_patterns.why: plugin-style deps (e.g. ray for modin, some driver backends) can be imported dynamically via entry points

verifications.description: Inventory document exists and lists every dep declared in pyproject.toml
verifications.expected: OK: all N deps present in inventory

verifications.description: No source files were modified under benchbox/

verifications.command: git diff --name-only HEAD -- pyproject.toml uv.lock | wc -l
verifications.description: pyproject.toml and uv.lock are untouched by this work

verifications.command:
uv run -- python -c "
import pathlib, sys
inv = pathlib.Path('docs/development/dependency-inventory.md').read_text()
flag_count = inv.count('FLAG-')
todos = list(pathlib.Path('_project/TODO/main/planning').glob('*dep*'))
if flag_count == 0: sys.exit('ERROR: no FLAG-* entries found in inventory')
if not todos: sys.exit('ERROR: no follow-up dep TODOs found in planning/')
print(f'OK: {flag_count} FLAG-* entries, {len(todos)} follow-up TODO(s)')
"
verifications.description: Inventory contains FLAG-* entries and at least one follow-up dep TODO exists in planning/
verifications.expected: OK: N FLAG-* entries, M follow-up TODO(s)

work_units.notes:
Parse `pyproject.toml` directly (tomllib) - do not use `uv pip list`
because it surfaces transitives. Include env markers (python_version,
sys_platform) in the captured row. Write raw table to
`docs/development/dependency-audit-raw.md`.
work_units.summary: Enumerate every declared dep from pyproject.toml (core, all extras, dependency-groups, tool.uv.sources). Capture name, version spec, owning group(s), inline rationale.

work_units.notes:
Handle package-name vs import-name mismatches: pyyaml→yaml,
psycopg2-binary→psycopg2, google-cloud-bigquery→google.cloud.bigquery,
beautifulsoup4→bs4, pillow→PIL, etc. Maintain the pkg→import map in
the inventory so future audits reuse it.
work_units.summary: Build import-site map for each declared dep: Grep `import <name>` / `from <name>` across benchbox/, scripts/, tests/, docs/. Record every file:line that imports each dep.

work_units.notes:
Ground truth for transitive reach is `uv tree`. Any "transitive-reach"
finding is fragile and becomes a candidate for promotion to an explicit
dep or removal of the dependent code path.
work_units.summary: Inverse check: find third-party imports in source that are NOT declared in pyproject.toml. Classify as (a) truly undeclared, (b) transitive-reach, or (c) stdlib misidentified.

work_units.notes:
Flag deps declared across multiple extras groups where one group
already transitively includes the other - consolidation candidates.
work_units.summary: Classify each declared dep by purpose (Core / SQL-adapter / Cloud-storage / DataFrame / Benchmark / Dev-test / Docs / MCP) and identify the owning benchbox module(s).

work_units.notes:
Evidence = import-site count from w2, owner module from w4, overlap
source for REDUNDANT. Verify plugin-style deps (ray for modin, entry-
point-loaded backends) before flagging UNUSED.
work_units.summary: Produce elimination candidate list per dep: KEEP, FLAG-UNUSED, FLAG-REDUNDANT, or FLAG-DEAD-EXTRA. Each FLAG entry gets a one-line justification + evidence.
Write docs/development/dependency-inventory.md - inventory table, elimination candidates with evidence, consolidation proposals, used-but-undeclared findings. Cross-link from AGENTS.md.
Create follow-up TODOs for each actionable finding - one per elimination/consolidation cluster. Each follow-up carries its own verification and must_preserve. This item does not perform removals.
